Objectives:
Objectives:
2
1. To immediately reduce hazardous fuel on the benches in the project area by removing all
mature and juvenile Pinon/Juniper on sage parks, to reduce juvenile trees by 90 % throughout,
and reduce the amount of shrub cover by 75-85% throughout. Tall mature oak brush with a basal
diameter of 5"or greater and an open under story would be left as wildlife and livestock habitat.
2. To increase the frequency of grasses and forbs by 20% over a 10 year period by decreasing the
number of encroached trees and reducing the cover of shrubs by 75-85%.
Planned_Implementation:
The proposed action is to reduce hazardous fuels caused by the overgrown
mountain shrub, sagebrush, and pinion-juniper encroachment on the sage/grass benches within
the project area. The treatment size would be approximately 400 acres, and treatment would be
with a heavy bladed drum (roller chopper, Lawson aerator etc.). The bladed drum is made of
heavy steel, which crushes and chops woody vegetation. It is pulled with a D-7 dozer or larger
with push bar or blade, or a large tractor with push bar or blade capable of handling this type of
vegetation. Prescribed fire may be used following the mechanical treatment to reduce fuel where
mechanical treatment is not possible due to terrain and if heavy fuels are left on the surface
needing removal for additional protection of natural resources, and oil and gas infrastructure.

Trt_Concerns_Desc:
A landscape of continuous hazardous fuels is
developing in the project area. Even though this project was not put forward as an urban
interface project there is substantial oil and gas infrastructure and development. This area is also
critical winter habitat for deer and elk. The shrub and grass/forb components have been
compromised by the shift in vegetation to overgrown mountain shrub type vegetation,
encroachment of pin yon/juniper onto sage/grass benches, and an increase in sage cover
compromising grass and forb production in sage parks. This in turn has decreased the amount of
palatable browse and forage for wildlife and livestock. Livestock use the allotment from 5/ 1-
12/1 however, dates may vary some depending upon forage availability. The grazing system
utilizes a three pasture deferred rotation. The shift in vegetation throughout the allotment has
concentrated livestock and wildlife in areas not vegetated by heavy shrub cover. This causes
some areas of the allotment to be used heavier than others. This treatment would help to reduce
heavy fuels in the area, increase available browse and forage for wildlife and livestock, distribute
grazing/browse use more evenly throughout the allotment, return the area to an earlier seral
stage, contribute to an overall healthier watershed, and protect oil and gas infrastructure.

Objectives:
Objectives:
1. To immediately reduce hazardous fuels in the treatment area by reducing tree cover by 75-
90%, and reduce the amount of shrub cover by 60-75%.
2. To increase the frequency of grasses and fo rbs by 10 % over a 10 year period by decreasing
the number of encroached shrubs and trees, and applying seed to the treatment areas.
Planned_Implementation:
The roller chopper is constructed of a heavy steel drum with blades, which crushes and chops
woody vegetation. It is pulled with a D-7 dozer or larger with a push bar or blade capable of
handling this type of vegetation. The treatment would allow for selective removal of vegetation,
keeping some large trees and islands for a mosaic landscape that would more closely resemble a
landscape where fire is a natural component of the ecosystem. Seeding would be done during the
treatment with a broadcast seeder mounted to the equipment so maximum seed incorporation
would occur. The seed mix would consist of cool season grasses and forbs. The treatment
would be contracted by the BLM, and mitigation identified by this analysis would be carried
forward as part of the contract Scope of Work. A baseline for monitoring would be established
before the project is implemented. Monitoring for measurable objectives would be carried out at
one year (minimum one growing season), three year, and 10 year intervals from implementation
to ensure that objectives are met and mitigation for invasive weeds is successful. If conditions
are identified at the third year monitoring indicating additional treatment for fuel hazard or weed
control is needed, additional measures may be conducted based on the analysis of this document.

Objectives:
General\xb7objectives of the project are as follows:

1 ).  Improve habitat for wildlife, including deer -and elk as well as improve forage
for livestock.
2).  Return the northwest portion of the Uncompahgre to a mosaic of successional stages
within the Pinon-Juniper and sagebrush communities. 
3 ).  Reduce the number of acres that are currently evaluated as being, or trending towards,
Condition Class ID on public lands to reduce the intensity of wildfires:.(See Attachment 6
for description of Fire Regime Condition-Classes -FRCC)
Planned_Implementation:
The roller chopper, a heavy bladed drum which crushes and chops woody vegetation, is pulled
by a D-8 bulldozer over the vegetation. The blade of the dozer is elevated two to three feet
above the ground surface to aid in laying vegetation over prior to roller chopping. As a result of
. the roller chopping, much of the woody vegetation would be chopped and crushed into small
sections and scattered along the soil surface. Depending on where the blades contact the plants
determines the effect on the plant. The majority of pinon and juniper trees would be chopped
and killed while others such as sagebrush and serviceberry are simply. laid over and remain alive,
resulting in a thinning effect. Treatment of oakbrush improves the diversity of age classes due
to the resprouting characteristic. The hydro-ax is a heavy duty mower mounted on a rubber tired
or tracked piece of equipment. Mowing results are similar to the rollerchopping. except more of
a patchy pattern is achieved along with a finer mulch on the ground surface.
